title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - D-6
notes:
West leads the ♦K against 2♠. West's ♦K wins the first trick and he continues with the ♦A and a diamond to East's ♦Q. East now leads the ♣9 to West's ♣A and West's ♣J return is taken by South. South leads a spade for a finesse, but West covers with the ♠K and dummy's ♠A wins the trick.

South must resist any temptation to draw the rest of the trump at this point. The lead is in the dummy for the first and last time. South must utilize this entry to play a heart toward the ♥KJ in the hope of playing that suit for a single loser. On the actual layout East has the ♥A and West has the ♥Q. South must play the ♥K in order to make his contract. If the heart honors are reversed, however, South must play the ♥J in order to hold his heart losers to 1.

West has already shown up with 15 HCP outside of hearts and if he was dealt the ♥A his hand would be too strong for a 1NT opening bid. It is possible, however, that East was dealt the the ♥A and that the ♥Q is with West. Therefore, South should rise with the ♥K if East follows low on the heart lead from dummy.
